references.text: This refers to the knowledge of God that is hidden and can only be revealed by God himself, which parallels how only the Father knows the Son and vice versa in Matthew 11:27.
This verse speaks of a hidden God, paralleling how Jesus describes the relationship between the Father and the Son as something known only to them.
This verse in Luke reflects the idea that only the Father knows the Son and vice versa, and that this knowledge can be revealed to whomever the Son chooses.
John speaks of no one having seen God, but the Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made him known, echoing the idea that only the Son can reveal the Father.
Hebrews begins by speaking of how God has spoken through the Son in these last days, pointing to the Son's unique role in revealing the Father.
